public_catalog_facts.description:
Compare nearby Bluetooth Low Energy signal strength while searching for an accessory you own or have permission to locate. The accessory must be actively advertising and visible to your iPhone.

A CLEARER WAY TO SEARCH
Start with the in-app guide: wake your accessory, choose by Bluetooth name and advertised manufacturer, then move a few slow steps and wait for fresh readings. A stronger signal alone does not identify your item.

LIVE MAP AND SIGNAL LIST
See device names, advertised manufacturers, and measured RSSI. When these details are unavailable, clear unnamed-device and manufacturer-unavailable labels explain what is missing. Stronger signals sit nearer the map center. Expand, pan, zoom, or choose a signal from the list. Dot angles are visual spacing, not compass directions.

COMPARE WITH CONFIDENCE
Follow smoothed strength, recent readings, and warmer-or-colder trends. Clear freshness and paused/lost states distinguish a live reading from historical data. Reset the comparison for another position. Pause, resume, and return to the signal list with direct controls. Haptic feedback can be switched off.

FREE AND PRIVATE
All features are free, without an account, subscription, or time limit. Scanning and analysis happen on your phone. Names and manufacturer identifiers are processed in memory on your phone. There is no location tracking, analytics, advertising, or signal upload.

UNDERSTAND THE LIMITS
RSSI is approximate relative signal strength, not exact distance. Walls, reflections, orientation, and transmit power affect results. Headphones, earbuds, and other accessories may stop advertising while asleep, connected, or in a closed case. Silent and powered-off devices cannot appear. Signal Scout does not verify people, device owners, or broadcast identity and does not replace an accessory maker's finding network.
